items.title: Non-empty bag shows "Empty bag" in the summary box below "Continue shopping"
covers: AC1: summary box has an "Empty bag" button below "Continue shopping"
items.reason: AC1 places the new button in a specific spot: inside the summary box and below "Continue shopping". A button rendered elsewhere (or above the link) would still let AC2 pass, so placement gets its own case. Only the rendered page shows placement, hence `e2e`.

items.title: "Empty bag" removes every product and shows the empty-bag state
covers: AC2: page shows "Your shopping bag is empty"
items.reason: AC2 is the story's core behaviour: one click removes every product, not just one. The bag has two different products, one with quantity 2, so a handler that removed only the first line or decremented a quantity would fail. The result is what the shopper sees, hence `e2e`.

items.title: Emptied bag is still empty after a page reload
covers: AC3: after reload the bag is still empty (emptied on the server)
items.reason: AC3 guards against a client-only clear: the page could show the empty state while the Basket service still holds the products. A full reload re-reads the basket from the server, so it is the observable proof of the server-side delete. Only a browser reload on the real stack shows it, hence `e2e` rather than a unit test of `BasketState`.

items.title: Empty bag shows no "Empty bag" button
covers: AC4: empty bag has no "Empty bag" button
items.reason: AC4 forbids the button on an empty bag. This case uses a bag that was never filled, so it checks the empty-state markup on its own, separately from the state reached by emptying (TC-PRB-19-02 and -03). The rendered page is the only place to see it, hence `e2e`.

items.title: Product lines, quantity controls, totals, "Check out" and "Continue shopping" are unchanged
covers: AC5: product lines, quantity controls, totals, "Check out" and "Continue shopping" unchanged
items.reason: AC5 requires that adding the button changes nothing else on the bag page. This case checks every listed element with exact values on a two-product bag, so a markup change that drops a control or breaks a total is caught. It is a rendered-page check, hence `e2e`.

items.title: Quantity stepper still updates a line and the totals
items.reason: AC5 keeps the quantity controls working. The new "Empty bag" form is a second enhanced form posted to the same page (`_handler=empty-cart` beside `update-cart`); a handler mix-up would make a quantity click empty the bag or do nothing. Clicking the stepper on the real page is the only way to prove the handlers stay separate, hence `e2e`.

items.title: Removing one product still removes only that line
items.reason: The story's motivation contrasts "Empty bag" with removing products one by one, and AC5 keeps that per-line removal unchanged. Removing one line must not empty the whole bag, and the "Empty bag" button must remain while a product is left. Separate from TC-PRB-19-06 because "Remove" posts quantity 0 and exercises a different path. Hence `e2e`.
